RELEASE CHANNEL
HAULING — FIELD MANUAL
TIPS & TRICKS
• Fresh shard first (server-hop) = fewer cargo desync bugs; check Shard Health on the System page.
• Test a freight elevator empty before loading — cargo can vanish on a reset.
• Autoload for contracts; manual tractor for commodities you bought.
• The Hull series retracts its cargo spine to fly/land, extends it to load — it is not dock-only. What differs per ship is how you load it (table below).
• Buy low / sell high — compare prices on the Hauling commodities list / UEX.
HOW-TO GUIDE
A. DOCK AT A STATION
1. Fly within 5–7 km of the station.
2. Open Comms → Landing Services → Request.
3. ATC assigns a pad / docking port / hangar by ship size.
4. Docking port: align until the ring + lines turn green (circle to SE, lines centered), then grow the square to match the circle.
5. Press [ N ] (default) to invoke docking — clamps engage.
B. REQUEST / WITHDRAW CARGO
Freight elevators are in hangars, station cargo decks, distribution-centre wings, and some outposts.
1. Look at the Freight Elevator terminal (no keybind — on-screen console).
2. Withdraw items from local inventory onto the cargo grid.
NOTE: for a hauling contract, the contracted cargo already shows on the terminal.
C. THREE WAYS CARGO GETS LOADED
1. CONTRACT AUTOLOAD: on a hauling contract the freight elevator already holds the cargo — pull your ship; at the destination the terminal auto-collects it → submit the contract.
2. MANUAL (by hand): for commodities you bought, or a ship parked at a station cargo deck, raise the cargo on the elevator and tractor-beam each SCU box onto your grid yourself (MaxLift / multi-tool; the ATLS exosuit is fastest).
3. PAID AUTO-LOAD: if the ship is in your hangar, you can pay a fee to have it loaded/unloaded for you instead of hand-loading. [community: ~10,000 aUEC load+unload; availability varies by site — not every ship/location offers it, and big freighters (Hull-C) load at the external station elevator.]
TIP: test the elevator empty first — if it resets with cargo on the grid, the cargo can vanish.
C2. BUYING & SELLING COMMODITIES
Buy: purchase at a commodity kiosk → the SCU is credited at that location → withdraw it onto the freight elevator / cargo grid → load onto your ship (manual, or paid auto-load if it's in your hangar).
Sell: land/dock at the buyer → unload onto the freight elevator/terminal → the sale registers and you're paid.
NOTE: small ships often load right at a pad's elevator; big freighters route through the large external elevators on a station cargo deck.
D. UNDOCK / DEPART
1. Retract landing gear ([ N ] default).
2. Press [ N ] (default) to undock / request departure.
Hangar takeoff: no turntable — come to a hover and yaw 180° to face the doors, then fly out on ATC clearance.
Your fable8 binds: Invoke Docking = Lshift+N, Landing gear = G.
E. HOW EACH SHIP LOADS (this is about LOADING access — not whether it can land)
ShipLoads viaNote
Hull-A / Hull-BLand + tractor / small elevatorSet down at outposts & pads; extend the cargo spine to load
Hull-CStation berth (spindle deployed)Can land (travel config — spindle retracted INSIDE the hull), but it can't load on its gear: the spindles are stowed inside. To load/unload it must deploy the spindle at a station berth + external freight elevator.
Hull-D / Hull-ENot flyable yet (4.8)Concept/lineup only — don't plan around them
C2 / M2 / A2 HerculesLand + pad/hangar elevatorPlanetary heavy cargo
CaterpillarLand + tractorModular freighter
Freelancer / Taurus / Cutlass / MSR / CorsairLand + tractor / elevatorSmall–medium haulers land at pads & outposts
Verified 4.8 (starcitizen.tools): Hull-C is no longer dock-only — it's shown landed/stored in hangars, and its folding cargo spindle (retract to fly, extend to load) is a real component. Hull-C open planet-surface landing is unconfirmed. Hull-D/E aren't confirmed flyable. The real per-ship difference is loading access (freight-elevator size / land-and-tractor), not landing.
F. TIPS & TRICKS
• Hull-C config [4.8 verified]: it folds the cargo spindle IN to fly/land (stores in an XL hangar) and OUT to load. KEY: it can't load while sitting on its landing gear — in landed config the spindles are stowed inside the hull, so loading/unloading only happens when it deploys the spindle at a station berth (external freight elevator). So it lands fine (not dock-only), but loading is station-only. Open planet-surface landing still unconfirmed.
• Squeeze extra SCU [community — risky]: loading MANUALLY by tractor beam, you can sometimes stack more than the rated SCU into open space as long as the grid isn't fully gridlocked (auto-snapped). Unsecured boxes can spill or despawn on a quantum jump or hard maneuver — not for valuable cargo.
• Move ONE box at a time [4.8 verified bug]: moving multiple items at once can desync inventory and lock the screen — transfer cargo singly.
• Fresh shard first: server-hop (log out/in) before a big haul; higher Server FPS = fewer cargo desync bugs. Check Shard Health (button on the System page) first.
• External elevators: use them where available and test empty first — if the grid resets with cargo on it, the cargo can vanish.
• Argo ATLS [community]: the ATLS loading exosuit speeds manual load/unload dramatically.
• Short loops stack: a 30k / 10-min run beats a 70k / 40-min run per hour. Confirm stock, price, demand and SELL capacity in the current server before loading a big hold — demand caps can strand cargo.
• Keep a reserve: keep 30–50% of your aUEC OUT of cargo so a lost run doesn't wipe you.
• Top off quantum fuel before long hauls; heavy, full ships burn more.

SALVAGE
SALVAGE — FIELD MANUAL
TIPS & TRICKS
• Blue hull sections are richest — scrape those first.
• Steady distance and angle beats upgrades for scrape speed.
• Master RMC (hull scraping) before moving to structural / CM.
• Grab loose components / cargo with a tractor beam for extra income.
• Vulture = solo single wrecks; Reclaimer = big multi-crew jobs.
HOW-TO GUIDE
A. SETUP & APPROACH
1. Find a wreck — Salvage contracts (Contract Manager), reclaim missions, or free-fly wrecks.
2. Pick the ship: Drake Vulture (solo, single wrecks), Aegis Reclaimer (large / multi-crew fleets).
3. Enter Salvage Mode (default [ M ]) and face the hull. RMB aims the beam(s); mouse wheel adjusts beam gap/focus.
B. HULL SCRAPING → RMC
1. In scrape mode, hold LMB and sweep the beam across the hull.
2. Read the panel outline: blue = rich, yellow = mediocre, red = nearly depleted.
3. Keep a stable distance and angle, work in zones, avoid chaotic boosting — technique beats upgrades for scrape speed.
4. Scraped material becomes RMC (Recycled Material Composite) in your ship's filler.
C. STRUCTURAL SALVAGE → CM ("munching")
1. Once the hull is stripped, switch to the disintegration / structural sub-mode.
2. Break down the remaining structure — this yields Construction Materials (CM).
NOTE: CM is the bigger industrial step. New to salvage? Master RMC scraping first, add CM once stable.
D. STORE, PACKAGE & SELL
1. The Filler forms RMC/CM into SCU boxes (Reclaimer fillers package 2 / 8 / 16 SCU).
2. Haul the boxes to a Trade / Commodity terminal and sell RMC / CM — check the Hauling tab / UEX for best price.
3. Loose components / cargo on the wreck: grab with a tractor beam (multi-tool / ATLS) and sell separately.
E. HAND SALVAGE
Small wrecks / stray panels: use the multi-tool + Cambio-SRT salvage attachment on foot — faster than repositioning a ship for stragglers.
NOTE: In-game keybinds shown are CIG defaults — verify yours on the Keybinds page.
MINING — FIELD MANUAL
TIPS & TRICKS
• Scan from a distance to read a rock's mass and composition % before you commit.
• Higher mass = more yield but needs more power / a bigger laser (or multi-crew MOLE).
• Keep the energy bar in the green; if it creeps toward red, back away — distance lowers power.
• Quantanium is the big earner but destabilizes over time — refine/sell it promptly.
• Refined ore usually sells for more than raw — refine, then check prices on the Hauling tab.
• Stubborn rock? Fit modules that cut resistance / instability.
HOW-TO GUIDE
A. FIND & SCAN
1. Fly to a mining area — asteroid cluster, planet/moon surface, or a cave for hand mining.
2. Use Scanning Mode (default [ V ]) to locate deposits, or just approach visible rocks.
3. Look at a rock to read its MASS (kg) and, up close, its mineral composition %.
NOTE: Mass class sets the tool — see the MASS REFERENCE table below.
B. FRACTURE — THE POWER WINDOW
1. Enter Mining Mode (default [ M ]).
2. Confirm FRACTURE mode — rock outline is yellow (= crack). Toggle fracture/extract with Left Alt + LMB.
3. Hold LMB to fire; raise power by scrolling the mouse wheel UP slowly.
4. Drive the rock's energy bar into the GREEN optimal window and hold it there.
CAUTION: Do NOT let the bar fill into the RED overcharge zone — the rock explodes and the yield is lost.
5. If it spikes toward red, lower power or back away (distance cuts effective power). Do not try to save it with more laser.
C. EXTRACT
1. After the rock fractures into chunks, switch to EXTRACT (Left Alt + LMB) — chunk outline turns purple.
2. Hold LMB to draw ore into your ship/backpack until the chunk is depleted.
3. Repeat per chunk. Full cargo/canister → head to a refinery.
D. REFINE & SELL
1. Dock at a refinery (e.g. an ARC-L / refinery deck) and use the Refinery Terminal.
2. Select your ore. The terminal lists every method side-by-side with its YIELD %, TIME, and COST — those change per material, so compare before you commit. Methods (yield ↔ speed ↔ cost tradeoff):
• Dinyx Solventation — highest yield, but slowest (long real-time timer). Best started before you log off.
• Pyrometric Chromalysis — above-average yield; higher cost, slow.
• Ferron Exchange — balanced compromise of yield / fee / time. Safe default.
• Electrostarolysis, Gaskin Process, Kazen Winnowing, Thermonatic Deposition, XCR Reaction — mid-range; yield/time/cost vary by ore — read the terminal.
• Cormack Method — fastest + cheapest, but lowest yield. Use when you need it now or the ore is cheap.
CAUTION: no method is best for everything — higher yield usually means slower + pricier. A refinery calculator (UEX) can pre-compute the best method + yield per ore.
3. Pay, wait for the timer, then collect refined SCU onto a hauler.
4. Sell refined ore at a Trade / Commodity terminal — check the Hauling tab / UEX for best price. Use the YIELD ESTIMATOR below to value a rock before you crack it.
NOTE: In-game keybinds shown are CIG defaults — verify yours on the Keybinds page. No danger to you; the only loss is an over-charged rock.

YIELD ESTIMATOR · PER-COMMODITY PAYOUT
WHAT THIS DOES: tells you what a mining rock is worth BEFORE you crack it.
1. Scan a rock in game — your scanner shows its size (mass/SCU) and what's inside (e.g. "Quantanium 12%").
2. Type the rock size into ROCK SIZE below.
3. Press [ + ADD ROW ] once per mineral — type its name, its % from the scanner, and the price/SCU (check the Trade Routes tab or UEX for current prices).
4. Read each mineral's payout and the GRAND TOTAL — that's the rock's value if you refine and sell everything. Rows save automatically.

BRAND CONFIG TOOLS — where you bind & calibrate

SETTINGS & CURVES — FLIGHT TIPS
General setup method — exact curve values depend on your hardware + feel. Community-sourced, verified 2026-07-14.
Deadzone — set only as much as needed so the axis rests at true center when released. Stiff spring / hard cam needs less; soft spring needs more.
Don't stack deadzones — if your VKB/VIRPIL/brand software already applies a deadzone, set the in-game deadzone to 0 (and vice-versa).
Curves / exponent — add an exponential response curve to soften the center for fine aim while keeping full deflection at the edges. Start subtle, raise to taste.
Saturation — if the gimbal can't reach software max travel, lower saturation; raise deadzone until it always reports center at rest.
Bind only the axes you need — pitch, yaw, roll + strafe (fwd/back, left/right). Everything else goes on buttons.
ESP (Enhanced Stick Precision) — SC's fine-aim assist near a target. Tune your sensitivity curve alongside it, not against it.
HOSAS vs HOTAS — dual sticks (HOSAS) give full 6DOF strafe; HOTAS leans on throttle-managed flight. Bind to match your layout.
Save on-device — VIRPIL / VKB / Azeron store profiles on the hardware, so binds survive a PC swap.
Tools: SC Launch Configurator (community, advanced per-axis curves) · Windows joy.cpl to confirm the OS sees full travel.
STAR CITIZEN CONTROL MAPPING
SC's keybindings live inside the game — no web link or URL can open them. Set bindings here:
Options → Keybindings → Advanced Controls Customization → [device / category]
To save or move a binding profile, SC reads/writes XML in this folder on the PC:
…\StarCitizen\LIVE\USER\Client\0\Controls\Mappings
In-game console (`): pp_rebindkeys export <name> writes the XML there; pp_rebindkeys <name> loads it back.
CRAFTING — FIELD MANUAL
HOW TO READ THIS. Crafting is new and CIG has published no 4.8-era guide. Their only official write-up is 4.7. So every line below is tagged: VERIFIED = official/primary source · COMMUNITY = credible but unofficial · UNCONFIRMED = nobody publishes it; do not bet aUEC on it.
A. THE LOOP
1. Buy an Item Fabricator (see C). Pull it from hangar storage at the freight console — search “FAB”. [COMMUNITY]

2. Move it with a tractor beam. It attaches to cargo grids, so it can ride in a ship. Placed in your hangar, it also reads your local inventory directly. [VERIFIED — CIG]

3. Get the materials into LOCAL INVENTORY. If they aren't there, the fabricator cannot see them. This is the #1 reason a new crafter thinks the machine is broken. [VERIFIED — CIG]

4. Pick a blueprint, assign materials (there are autofill / best / worst buttons), watch the live stat preview, choose a delivery location, hit Fabricate. [VERIFIED — CIG]

5. Crafting and dismantling run separate simultaneous queues; finished jobs land in a history log. [VERIFIED — CIG]

Blueprints are account-bound and permanent once acquired — they survive death. From mission rewards (low drop rate), reputation, loot crates, or purchase. [VERIFIED — CIG]
Craft times and any aUEC job fee: [UNCONFIRMED] — CIG says only that time scales with size and quality. No source publishes real numbers.
B. BIG ITEMS — SHIP COMPONENTS & SHIP WEAPONS
STRAIGHT ANSWER: this is undocumented. Nobody has published it.
You asked how you get out an item too big to carry out of the fabricator by hand. I could not verify it, so I am not going to invent it.
What is actually known:

• Ship-component and ship-weapon blueprints DO exist in 4.8, datamined straight from the game files. [COMMUNITY — RSI Community Hub blueprint finder, 4.8 files]

• The fabricator has its own internal cargo grid “for the input and output of resources and items.” [VERIFIED — CIG, direct quote]

• The craft flow includes a “choose delivery location” step — but no source lists what the options are. [UNCONFIRMED] That dropdown is almost certainly where your answer lives.

• No size or SCU gate is documented anywhere. The string “SCU” does not appear in CIG's crafting guide at all. [UNCONFIRMED]

• Do not assume ASOP. 4.8.0 added Item Recovery for vehicle loadouts via ASOP, but no source connects that to crafting. [UNCONFIRMED]

MY BEST GUESS, LABELLED AS A GUESS: output physicalises onto the fabricator's own cargo grid, and you tractor it off like any other cargo. That follows from the quoted “input and output” line — but it is inference, not a sourced fact.

SOURCES CONFLICT — read this before you spend money: CIG's 4.7 guide lists vehicle components and weapons as a FUTURE expansion, yet the 4.8 files contain those blueprints. Both can be true (shipped after the guide was written), but CIG never published a 4.8 crafting guide and the 4.8.0 patch notes do not mention crafting at all.

There is no personal-vs-industrial fabricator split in LIVE. One machine exists. Food, Medical and Construction fabricators are explicitly in development — the Construction one, at hangar scale, is what will craft ships. In-vehicle crafting machines are also in development. [VERIFIED — CIG]
C. WHERE TO BUY A FABRICATOR
One model exists: the RediMake Item Fabricator (KE Group). There are no fabricator tiers. [VERIFIED]
Average ~99,771 aUEC across 22 terminals. [COMMUNITY — UEX, 4.8.x]

CHEAPEST: 95,001 aUEC — Tammany and Sons, Metro Center, Lorville (Hurston). Only 4.8.3-stamped price on the board.
• 99,990 — Kel-To, Aspire Grand, New Babbage (microTech); Refinery Shop ARC-L1; Refinery Shop HUR-L1
• 100,000 — Dumper's Depot Area 18, and most Refinery Shops / Pyro / Nyx terminals

CAUTION — RESALE: the only sell-back seen is 35,980 aUEC at MIC-L1. That's roughly a 64% loss. Buy it once, in the right place. [COMMUNITY — UEX]

WARNING — THE 100K TRAP: a fabricator left deployed can disappear from your hangar. Stow it on the freight elevator when you're done. Widely reported. [COMMUNITY]
D. ORE QUALITY → GEAR QUALITY
CORRECTION — this tablet previously had this wrong. The bands are driven by the ore's QUALITY value, not its DENSITY. Density isn't even a per-rock stat — a rock's stats are Mass, Instability and Resistance. “Density” in mining talk means how concentrated a material is at a location. The old “not resistance” half was right; the “density” half was a conflation.
Every resource carries a quality value 0–1000, and that value determines the traits of anything crafted from it. [VERIFIED — CIG, direct quote]
Quality can only be read up close in mining mode — rock type scans from range, quality does not. [COMMUNITY]
Refining preserves quality. Mixing qualities averages the finished item. [VERIFIED — CIG]

THE 8 BANDS — ore in a band all snaps to the same quality value: [COMMUNITY — Scopique, reporting 4.8 PTU notes]
BandSource rangeSnaps to (IRON)
10–399325

TWO CAVEATS OR THIS TABLE WILL MISLEAD YOU:
1. These snap values are IRON-specific. The rule says each ore type has its own value per band, so copper's band 2 is probably NOT 521. A per-ore table does not exist publicly. [UNCONFIRMED]
2. The source is a blog reporting leaked 4.8 PTU notes — not CIG, and not confirmed against 4.8 LIVE. [UNCONFIRMED vs LIVE]
E. WHAT BANDS FOR MAX GEAR
q500 is the break-even. At 500 your crafted item matches what you'd buy off an NPC shelf. Below 500 you get penalties; above 500, bonuses. [COMMUNITY] — note the number 500 appears nowhere in CIG's own guide; this is community-derived.

Worked example (P4-AR + iron): q325 → −2.62% impact, −4.2% fire rate. q710 → +3.15% impact, +5.84% fire rate. [COMMUNITY — 4.7 data]

MAX GEAR = BAND 8 (999–1000). No cap is documented — higher appears to be better all the way to 1000. [UNCONFIRMED that any cap exists]

THE THING THAT ACTUALLY CHANGES HOW YOU MINE (synthesis, not a sourced claim):
The bands create hard plateaus. A q899 rock and a q800 rock both snap to 874 — identical gear. So quality gained within a band is worth nothing. The only thing that pays is crossing into the next band.
And the bands collapse at the top: Band 1 spans 400 points; Band 8 spans 2. Band 8 will be brutally rare — chasing it is a lottery, while Band 4 (700+) is the realistic target for good gear.
Rules of thumb: most rocks land 200–600; Stanton commonly 350–450; Pyro runs better; 800+ is rare and 900+ takes serious dedication. [COMMUNITY]
F. TRAPS & THINGS THAT AREN'T IN YET
• Dismantling returns shop/loot items at default quality 500. Player-crafted items return the quality you built them with, but less of it — material is lost in manufacture and teardown. This is the only waste mechanic. [VERIFIED — CIG]

• Variant gear generally can't be dismantled — basic/non-variant only. [COMMUNITY]

• Craft failure chance: no source mentions any. [UNCONFIRMED]

• Crafted-gear persistence / insurance: CIG documents this for blueprints only. Gear is [UNCONFIRMED]. Note 4.8.0 shipped a full character wipe, the first since 4.0. [VERIFIED]

• NOT IN THE GAME YET (all future-tense in CIG's guide): item degradation & repair, catalysts, blueprint tiers & research (T1–3, vehicles to T5), datapad blueprints, a blueprint library app, player trading of materials, the new alloy/byproduct refining system, salvage integration. [VERIFIED — CIG]

• CIG's own hedge: “blueprint requirements are subject to change in future patches.” [VERIFIED]
YOU CAN CLOSE THE BIGGEST GAP YOURSELF. One screenshot of the fabricator's “delivery location” dropdown would settle the big-item question that no source on the internet currently answers. Snap it and this manual gets a verified section B.
